Oral sodium bicarbonate was also added for the treatment of normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. The patient's hyperphosphatasemia, hypophosphatemia, and metabolic acidosis gradually improved, and his lower limb pain did not recur. His kidney function was almost unchanged, but the level of urinary β2-microglobulin remained high over the following two years (Figure). The pan-aminoaciduria, glycosuria, and hypouricemia were not completely ameliorated.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old Japanese man with chronic HBV infection presented with an 11-year history of low-dose adefovir dipivoxil (ADV) 10 mg daily (June 2005 to 2016). He was referred for CKD management (creatinine 1.84 mg/dL, eGFR 29.7) during preoperative evaluation for hepatocellular carcinoma, with treatment-resistant joint pain and osteomalacia previously attributed to vitamin D deficiency. Laboratory evaluation revealed Fanconi syndrome: hypophosphatemia (1.6 mg/dL) with inappropriate renal phosphate wasting (fractional excretion 79.3%), hypouricemia (1.6 mg/dL) with uricosuria (FE 69.3%), glycosuria (4+) despite modest hyperglycemia (184 mg/dL), pan-aminoaciduria, proximal renal tubular acidosis (HCO3- 14.6 mmol/L), and markedly elevated urinary β2-microglobulin (66,919 μg/L). Osteomalacia was confirmed radiographically by multiple Looser zones in metatarsals and proximal tibias, with hyperphosphatasemia (1,148 IU/L). Crucially, 25-hydroxyvitamin D was normal (18 ng/mL, range 7-41), excluding vitamin D deficiency as the cause. ADV was discontinued and switched to entecavir. Following discontinuation, hyperphosphatasemia, hypophosphatemia, and metabolic acidosis gradually improved, and lower limb pain did not recur, establishing causality. Kidney function remained stable, though some tubular defects (pan-aminoaciduria, glycosuria, hypouricemia, elevated β2-microglobulin) persisted partially over two years of follow-up.
